title: Big Storms Delay Holiday Travel and the Macy's Parade
summary:
Thanksgiving travel ran into big storms this year. Strong storms swept across the United States on Thursday, November 26. They brought heavy rain, strong winds, and snow in the Midwest. Flooding hit the California coast. About 81.5 million people were expected to travel, and hundreds of flights were cancelled or delayed by Thursday morning.

On the West Coast, very high tides called king tides flooded streets. They knocked off part of Pacifica Pier, and people were told to leave. On the East Coast, weather expert Richard Bann warned of wind, rain, and flooding. The East Coast storm was expected to clear out by Saturday.

The weather also changed parade plans. In New York City, Mayor Zohran Mamdani said the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade would move to Saturday, November 28. It would have been the parade's 100th, with a record 100 giant balloons. This is the first time in 100 years it will happen on a day other than Thanksgiving. Mamdani said safety came first, with winds gusting up to 65 miles per hour.
why_it_matters: Storms can change holiday plans, so knowing the weather helps families travel safely and still enjoy the fun.
